page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads per core on a dedicated basis. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates a strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 25% at 2923.48. However, multi-core performance is weak, with stress-ng multi-core scoring in the bottom 25% at 2928.18. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the passmark memory score and cached small-block read bandwidth of 136.13 GB/sec both rank in the bottom 10%. Text processing and single-threaded decompression tasks show average performance, while database operations and Redis SET operations fall into the bottom 10%.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it an entry-level option for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation without high memory bandwidth demands. The primary tradeoff is the low multi-core scaling and weak memory throughput, which limits its utility for memory-intensive or highly parallelized tasks. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, text processing, or small-scale development and testing environments.
